The app helps you never miss birthdays, anniversaries, memorials and special events, and send greetings on time.
• Add an event with the "Add event" button: you can simply type the date in your own words (Hebrew text is understood).
• Every event gets ready-made reminders for its type; you can change them any time.
• "Groups" (in Settings) set reminders, a greeting and a distribution list at once for family, friends and work.
• Already have data? Import from contacts or from the phone's calendars (in Settings).
• The ? button on every screen explains it, and a long press on an icon says what it does.

This is the home screen: what is coming and when, with a countdown.
• Tap an event to open it. Long press: "Show in calendar".
• The type chips at the top filter; you can pick several together.
• The options button (sliders) opens grouping, sorting and advanced filters: tags, groups, date range and milestones only.
• "Milestones" are round ages, silver and golden anniversaries, Bar and Bat Mitzvah.
• Your choices are saved, and you can restore the defaults from the options.

In the list's view settings:
• Grouping: by proximity, day, week, Gregorian or Hebrew month, type, tag, group or age decade. An event with several tags or groups appears in each.
• Sorting: by date, name, type, age or years, recently added or recently updated, ascending or descending. An item without a value (for example no age) is always last.
• Filtering: several conditions together: all of them must hold.
• The date range applies to each event's next occurrence. To see distant years also set "Until date".

Five views: agenda, day, week, month and year.
• Move between periods with the arrows, or swipe sideways. "Today" returns to today.
• Tapping the title (for example the month name) opens a month and year picker in two taps.
• Magnifier: jump to an event by name. Calendar icon: jump to a date.
• Pinch with two fingers to switch levels: from month to day and back.
• In the menu you can hide or show events, holidays and the weekly portion. The last view is remembered.

Pick a type: it determines the matching calendar (a memorial is counted in the Hebrew calendar) and the initial reminders.
• Name: for a birthday, memorial and Bar/Bat Mitzvah it is also the person's name.
• Date: type it freely, pick from the calendar, or pick a Hebrew month and day. The date is always shown in both calendars.
• "The year is known": without a year, age and number of years are not calculated.
• "After sunset": if someone was born after dark, the Hebrew date is that of the next day.
• Color, emoji, photo, tags and groups help you organize and find.

Type the date the way you would say it, and the app understands (in Hebrew):
• "17 באוקטובר 1980", "17.10.80", "1980-10-17"
• "כ׳ בחשוון תשמ״ז", "י״ג באלול", "14 באדר ב׳"
• Age: "בת 46, נולדה ב-17 באוקטובר": the birth year is calculated.
• Weekday: "נולד ביום שלישי...": if it does not match the date you get a warning. Without a year, a list of matching years is shown to choose from.
• "אחרי השקיעה" or "בלילה" marks a birth after dark.
The result appears immediately in both calendars and can be corrected with the pickers below.

Everything about one event: dates in both calendars, next occurrences, age or years, Bar/Bat Mitzvah Shabbat and portion.
• "Send greeting" opens the greetings screen.
• Reminders: a switch to turn on and off, and a button for editing and suggestions.
• Checklist and gifts: preparation tasks and a gift budget.
• The menu at the top: edit, archive and delete. Archive hides without deleting.
• After a delete an "Undo" button appears for a few seconds: it restores the event with its reminders, list and groups.

Every reminder is: how long before, at what time, and on which channel.
• The "Notification" channel notifies; WhatsApp, e-mail and SMS are "time to greet" reminders that open the greeting ready.
• For a Hebrew event you can choose "At nightfall", so it reminds at the right time, and for a Gregorian one "After midnight".
• Shabbat and holidays: a reminder can be moved to before Shabbat starts, after it ends, to both, or skipped.
• "Only at milestones" limits a reminder to a round birthday, silver anniversary and the like.
• "Send to": the person, me, groups (their distribution list) and extra numbers: up to 30 recipients, each once.
• On the SMS channel you can choose "Send the greeting by itself": it needs SMS permission and may cost money depending on your plan.
• If notifications do not arrive, check "Reminder health" in Settings.

Pick a template, adjust the wording and send with one tap.
• The name, age, dates and portion fill in by themselves. A part in double brackets appears only if it has data.
• Recipient: the person, myself, or another number or e-mail.
• WhatsApp, e-mail and another app open with the message ready: you need to press send yourself. There is no legitimate way to send on WhatsApp without a tap.
• Sending to several people: pick "Distribution list": each recipient gets their own message with one tap (write {נמען} to address each by name), or an SMS to everyone at once after confirmation.
• Below the text are emoji that suit the event: tap to add to the message. You can also attach a photo from the gallery: it is sent to WhatsApp with the text as a caption.
• Voice message: record and send to a chat.
• Song ideas open as a search.
• Your own templates are saved in Settings → Greeting templates: in folders, with tags and group assignment. You can style the inserted details (bold, color, a character between letters) and the style adapts to WhatsApp, e-mail and plain messages.

A group is a circle of people: family, friends, work, partner, children, parents, and you can add your own.
• For each group: color, emoji, tags added to members, a reminder template, a preferred greeting and channel, and a distribution list.
• "Apply to members" sets the reminder template on every member of the group. A reminder you edited on the event itself is not overwritten.
• An event can be in several groups. When it joins a group it gets the group's tags and reminders.
• The main list can be filtered and grouped by group.

Every event has a list of preparations and gifts.
• A task can get "days before the event": the due date is counted back from the next occurrence, and an overdue task is highlighted.
• Gift: enter a budget; when you mark it bought, the amount counts as paid.
• "Add a ready list" gives a start based on the event type.
• "Start over" clears all marks for next year.
• You can also tick from the home screen widget.

Search names, notes and tags, Hebrew and Gregorian dates, ranges and types.
• You can write in natural Hebrew, for example "ימי הולדת בחודש הבא".
• "Search within a search" narrows the results step by step.
• Useful searches are saved, and there are automatic suggestions by pattern.

Add from the phone's home screen: long press → Widgets → PresentSimple.
• Upcoming events: a list with a countdown; on today's event there is a "Greeting" link straight to the send screen.
• Event and checklist: pick an event and tick tasks right from the screen.
• Today's date: Hebrew and Gregorian and the next event.
• Mini month: days with events are marked; tapping a day opens a new event on that date.
Widgets update at midnight and on every change. In Settings → Security you can hide names and list items in them.

Settings → Backup and sharing.
• A backup to a file includes events, reminders, checklists, groups and templates. Photos are not included.
• Password encryption: a forgotten password cannot be recovered.
• Restore shows what will be added before anything changes: add without duplicates, or replace everything.
• Files with the .sevents extension open straight from WhatsApp or the file manager.
• Sharing selected events: as a file that someone who has the app is offered to save (and chooses which), or as a tidy message for WhatsApp and e-mail. You choose which details join: notes, phone, tags, reminders, checklist and groups.
• Automatic backup to a folder you choose (daily, weekly or monthly), with a number of copies to keep.
• Import from a spreadsheet (CSV): the app recognizes columns by their headers, understands dates in any format, and shows a preview.
• Export to a calendar (ICS) and a spreadsheet (CSV), and sharing the app itself as an install file.
• The file contains names and phone numbers in plain text: keep it somewhere safe.

Settings → Calendar sync.
• Save to Google Calendar: pick a Google calendar on the device and turn on automatic sync: events are written to the calendar and updated by themselves. In the event editor you can decide per event: follow settings, save to calendar, or don't save. Each entry is marked in its description so the app recognizes it, and Google syncs it to the cloud and to your other devices.
• Import: pick calendars and scan. Entries saved by the app are restored exactly; others are recognized by name (birthdays, anniversaries, memorials). When an entry is similar to or conflicts with something that exists you see a comparison and choose: create new, merge with the existing, or ignore.
• Dedicated calendar: creates a separate "אירועים מיוחדים" calendar on the phone with all events for 5 years, including the Hebrew date. You can refresh or remove it.
• Calendar permission is required. Saving to Google Calendar sends Google the event's name and date (not notes) through the device's calendar sync.

• Settings are grouped by topic: tap a title to open or close it.
• Appearance: light, dark or system, and dynamic color.
• Calendar: Hebrew, Gregorian or both; in Israel or abroad; Sunday as the first day.
• Yearly date rules: what to do in Adar of a leap year, on the 30th of Cheshvan/Kislev when it does not exist, and on February 29.
• Reminders: place (for nightfall and Shabbat times), reminder health and permissions.
• Greetings: my phone and e-mail, and the country prefix.
• Security: lock the app with the device lock (with a timeout of your choice), and hide it from the recent apps list and screenshots. You can also hide details in widgets.
• Each group has "Restore defaults", and there is a global reset.
• Reminders: you can turn on a daily morning summary: one notification with today's and tomorrow's events.
• Updates: check, download and install a new version straight from the app (a regular update; your data is kept). You can keep an automatic check once a day, and share a download link on WhatsApp or by e-mail.

Four kinds of printing, all with a preview:
• Greeting card: pick an event, a text and a design (classic, festive, simple), with or without a photo and dates. You can also share it as an image.
• Monthly calendar: the whole month with events, holidays and the weekly portion: Hebrew, Gregorian or both according to the calendar setting.
• Yearly calendar: 12 months on one page for hanging: days with events are marked and the list of events is under each month.
• List: all birthdays and dates of a year, filtered by type, group and tag, and grouped by month, type or group.
Printing opens the device's print window: from there you can print or choose "Save as PDF". Page size: A4 or A5.
Before the app opens, the device lock is requested: a code, password, pattern or fingerprint / face. The app does not see or store them.
To turn on the lock, first set a screen lock on the device (Settings → Security).

Data is stored only on the device. The app connects to the internet only when you check for an update, and sends no personal information to any server; names in notifications on a locked screen are hidden; the log contains no names. Widgets show events even while the app is locked.
The app saves a backup to a folder you choose (for example in your cloud) regularly, and keeps only the latest copies. The files are not encrypted: choose a folder you trust.
